claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy is single-phase bcc.
The initial alloy has a random atomic distribution with no significant chemical short-range order.
High-temperature annealing induces the formation and percolation of SRO clusters.
Interatomic potentials used to model the intervention must be parameterized to reproduce the SRO-evolution energy landscape.
The single-phase bcc structure is stable above 1000 K.
SRO clusters reach a critical volume fraction at which they form a percolating network.
A percolating SRO network can act as a distinct phonon-transport channel or scattering barrier depending on its coherence length relative to the phonon mean free path.
Percolating SRO creates a connected sub-lattice with vibrational properties distinct from those of the surrounding alloy.
The SRO network may have modified force constants or locally reduced mass disorder.
The connected SRO network permits coherent phonon propagation that counteracts scattering from isolated SRO clusters.
SRO percolation produces a nonlinear transition in thermal conductivity.
The conductivity transition may appear as a sudden increase or a plateau at the critical SRO-percolation threshold.
The predicted conductivity response deviates from serial or parallel mixing rules and simple scattering models.
Standard mixing and point-defect scattering models predict a gradual monotonic reduction in thermal conductivity as SRO-related disorder increases.
The proposed mechanism applies only when SRO clusters physically percolate within a single-phase bcc alloy.
The proposed mechanism does not apply when SRO remains isolated or phase separation occurs.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome restrict the anomaly to an increase or plateau, whereas the uncertainty field states that even the sign of the conductivity change, including increase versus decrease, is unresolved.
